prompt: Which statement correctly defines an elastic collision between two bodies?
options: A collision in which the total kinetic energy of the system is the same before and after the collision
A collision in which total linear momentum is conserved while kinetic energy decreases
A collision in which the colliding bodies stick together and move off with a common velocity
A collision in which no contact forces act between the colliding bodies

answer.explanation: An elastic collision is defined strictly as a collision in which the total kinetic energy of the system is conserved (remains unchanged before and after the impact).

distractor_explanations: Correct: this matches the official Cambridge physics definition of an elastic collision.
Incorrect: momentum is conserved in all collisions in isolated systems; a collision where kinetic energy decreases is an inelastic collision.
Incorrect: when bodies stick together, the collision is completely inelastic (coalescent).
Incorrect: contact forces (Newton's third law interaction pairs) act during every physical collision regardless of elasticity.
hints: Recall the exact physical quantity that distinguishes an elastic collision from an inelastic collision.
Is momentum conserved in both types of collision?
solution: Option 1 is correct. By definition, an elastic collision is one in which the total kinetic energy of the system is the same before and after the collision.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Distinguish between linear momentum and kinetic energy.
Step 2: Momentum is conserved in any isolated collision (elastic or inelastic).
Step 3: The defining property of an elastic collision is that total kinetic energy is also conserved.
